title: A pipeline destroys an existing PIPE1.$$$ file
steps: Boot followup with multi-boot-fixture.img and followup-fixture.img. CD \T; TYPE PIPE1.$$$; TYPE ONE.TXT | SORT; DIR PIPE1.$$$; TYPE PIPE1.$$$.
observed: The sentinel USER-OWNED-PIPE-FILE is readable before the pipe. The pipe prints ALPHA, then the sentinel file is gone. The stopped-image extraction also has no PIPE1.$$$.
expected: Choose an unused temporary name and preserve existing files (tester expectation for temporary-file handling; original DOS Reference pp.132-135 describes pipes).

title: Output to a full disk silently becomes an empty file
steps: Boot re-full0 with multi-boot-fixture.img and full0-fixture.img. CD \T; DIR /W; ECHO TEST > FULL.OUT; DIR FULL.OUT; TYPE FULL.OUT.
observed: DIR reports 0 bytes free. ECHO returns without an error; FULL.OUT exists with zero bytes instead of TEST plus CR/LF. The source files remain intact.
expected: Report a disk-full write error; do not silently discard requested output (tester expectation; DOS Reference redirection pp.132-135).

title: A pipeline on a full disk silently loses its input
steps: On the same full0 fixture, CD \T; TYPE ONE.TXT | SORT; ECHO PIPE-RETURNED.
observed: The pipe prints nothing and no error. PIPE-RETURNED appears normally. ONE.TXT contains ALPHA plus CR/LF. Repeated after filling the last 512 bytes in re-full512.
expected: Print ALPHA or report failure to create/write the pipe intermediate (tester expectation; DOS Reference pp.132-135).

title: COPY reports Bad command for a disk-full write
steps: On full0-fixture.img, CD \T; COPY LONG.TXT FULL.BIN; DIR FULL.BIN.
observed: COPY prints Bad command or file name and leaves a zero-byte FULL.BIN. LONG.TXT exists and is 76800 bytes.
expected: A disk-space/write failure diagnostic identifying why COPY failed; command syntax and source are valid (tester expectation).

title: A long batch file silently stops before its final command
steps: Boot suite4 with multi-boot-fixture.img and suite-fixture.img; run \CASES\B063.BAT. It CALLs BIG.BAT, which contains BIG-BEGIN, 65 long REM lines, and BIG-END.
observed: BIG-BEGIN and the caller's BIG-RETURNED print, but BIG-END never executes; no limit/error is reported.
expected: Run the complete batch or explicitly reject it. InitechDOS Reference ch4-batch.tex:19-25 describes a batch as a sequence of commands, with no file-size restriction. Suspected cause (guess): os/milton/command.c:4212 BATCH_FILE_MAX=4096.

title: SHIFT loses arguments after the ninth
steps: Run \CASES\B060.BAT, or TEN one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven on more-fixture.img.
observed: The original ninth argument is nine. After SHIFT, %9 is empty; ten and eleven never become available.
expected: Shift later arguments into %9 (DOS Reference printed p.151, PDF236). The Initech manual explicitly limits initial arguments to nine, but this is a DOS compatibility gap.

title: SHIFT changes %0 contrary to the shipped manual
steps: Run \CASES\B060.BAT with its eleven arguments.
observed: ZERO initially identifies the batch path; after SHIFT, ZERO=one.
expected: The shipped Reference ch4-batch.tex:247 says "%0, the name of the batch file, is not changed." Actual shifting of %0 agrees with original DOS p.151; fix the manual contract rather than changing DOS-compatible behavior.

title: A path-qualified batch name requires the .BAT extension
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; A:\T\BATCH2; A:\T\BATCH2.BAT; BATCH2.
observed: The first form says Bad command or file name. Both controls print BATCH2-RAN.
expected: Resolve .BAT for a qualified name as for a bare name. InitechDOS Reference ch4-batch.tex:32 says to type the name without its extension; original DOS batch invocation uses drive/path forms.

title: COMMAND without /C cannot open a nested prompt
steps: Boot followup; type COMMAND. Then try COMMAND /C COMMAND /C ECHO NESTED.
observed: Bare COMMAND says Invalid number of parameters. Nested /C works and prints NESTED.
expected: Start a secondary command processor and allow EXIT back to the caller. InitechDOS Reference ch2-entries-b.tex:102-104 promises typing commands in a second copy; DOS Reference COMMAND pp.46-47.

title: COMMAND /C loses its child program exit status
steps: Boot advanced-misc (geometry-boot-fixture.img, more-fixture.img); CD \T; ERR0.COM; COMMAND /C ERR7.COM; IF ERRORLEVEL 7 ECHO CHILD-EXIT7; IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 7 ECHO CHILD-STATUS-LOST. Run ERR7.COM directly as a control.
observed: The /C form prints CHILD-STATUS-LOST; the direct form prints DIRECT-EXIT7. ERR7.COM exits through INT 21h/AH=4Ch with AL=7.
expected: Propagate the child status so ERRORLEVEL can test it (tester DOS command-processor expectation; Reference IF p.147 and Initech ch4-batch.tex:185-186).

title: CD drive: does not display that drive's current directory
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; CD C:\CHOME; CD D:\DHOME; CD C:; CD D:; CD.
observed: Both drive-only queries are silent; CD alone still prints A:\T. Drive-relative file access and switching drive show that per-drive directories were set.
expected: Display C:\CHOME and D:\DHOME without switching drives (DOS Reference printed p.42/PDF127).

title: ATTRIB cannot find a readable file on D:
steps: Boot advanced-driveutils; CD \T; TYPE D:\DHOME\SAME.TXT; ATTRIB D:\DHOME\SAME.TXT; ATTRIB +R D:\DHOME\SAME.TXT.
observed: TYPE prints D-DRIVE. Both ATTRIB forms print Invalid path (or file not found).
expected: Read and set attributes on the specified mounted drive. InitechDOS Reference ch2-entries-a.tex:9-12 accepts a drive-qualified file.

title: CHKDSK reports a FAT error on valid C: and D: volumes
steps: Boot advanced-driveutils using the geometry-corrected boot fixture; CHKDSK C:; CHKDSK D:. Compare ordinary DIR/TYPE/COPY operations on those volumes.
observed: Both checks say Disk error reading (or writing) FAT. The same volumes support file reads and writes. CHKDSK on A: works.
expected: Check the requested mounted FAT12 volume; do not report a disk error simply for its drive letter (DOS CHKDSK and InitechDOS Reference ch2-entries-a.tex, CHKDSK).

title: TREE ignores an explicit other-drive operand
steps: Boot suite4; CD \T; CD D:\DHOME; TREE D: /F. Also TREE D:\DHOME /F in followup.
observed: TREE D: lists volume INITECH and A:\T contents. The absolute D: form says Invalid path despite the directory being readable with TYPE.
expected: Walk the specified drive/path and label that volume (InitechDOS Reference ch2-entries-c.tex:125-140).

title: LABEL rejects a valid mounted D: volume
steps: Boot suite4; VOL D:; LABEL D: NEWLABEL.
observed: VOL displays EXTRA, but LABEL returns Invalid drive specification.
expected: Apply the label to the requested valid drive (DOS LABEL; InitechDOS Reference ch2-entries-b.tex LABEL drive parameter).

title: FIND ignores filename operands and waits for keyboard input
steps: Boot suite2; run \CASES\B032.BAT, whose first command is FIND "Alpha" LINES.TXT. Wait 12 seconds; or run that command directly from A:\T.
observed: No search results or file header appear; FIND waits for standard input. Ctrl-Z plus Enter returns. FIND "Alpha" < LINES.TXT works.
expected: Open the named input file (DOS Reference pp.72-73/PDF157-158). Initech documentation only describes redirection; this is a compatibility gap.

title: FIND returns success when no line matches
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; FIND "absent" < ONE.TXT; IF ERRORLEVEL 1 ECHO RC1; IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 1 ECHO RC0.
observed: No line matches, but RC0 is printed.
expected: Return 1 when no matching line exists, 0 when a match exists (tester DOS FIND exit-status memory; distinguish from malformed-argument status).

title: FIND stops its search string at the first embedded quote
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; FIND "He said ""yes""" < QUOTES.TXT.
observed: Both He said "yes" and He said no are printed, as if searching only for He said .
expected: Match the embedded quoted word, returning only the first line (DOS Reference pp.72-73/PDF157-158, quotation-mark handling).

title: FIND silently accepts an unknown switch
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; FIND /BAD "ALPHA" < ONE.TXT.
observed: It prints ALPHA with no invalid-switch diagnostic.
expected: Reject an unsupported switch with a useful error (tester expectation; valid switches listed on DOS p.72).

title: SORT /+n ignores the requested starting column
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; SORT /+4 < SORTCOL.TXT. The input is 01 zebra then 02 apple.
observed: The output remains 01 zebra then 02 apple.
expected: Sort apple before zebra starting at column 4 (DOS Reference printed p.116/PDF201).

title: TIME rejects hundredths of a second
steps: Boot suite3; run \CASES\B039.BAT, or TIME 13:14:15.99.
observed: Invalid time; previous time remains unchanged.
expected: Accept the .hundredths field (DOS Reference p.120/PDF205). The narrower shipped Initech syntax does not promise it; this is DOS compatibility.

title: VERIFY is unavailable
steps: Boot stock or suite3; VERIFY; VERIFY ON; VERIFY OFF.
observed: All forms say Bad command or file name.
expected: Provide the DOS write-verification switch and state query (DOS Reference p.125/PDF210). COPY /V is separately implemented.

title: ECHO. cannot emit a blank line
steps: Boot suite3; run \CASES\B036.BAT, or type ECHO. at the prompt.
observed: Bad command or file name.
expected: Output a blank line (tester DOS 3.x memory; no claim this shorthand is specified in the shipped manual).

title: ECHO OFF at the prompt prints OFF and leaves echo on
steps: Boot advanced-keyboard; ECHO OFF; ECHO; ECHO ON.
observed: OFF is printed as ordinary text; the query still says ECHO is on. The batch form does change state.
expected: Change echo state at the prompt too (tester DOS memory; DOS Reference p.143 documents ON/OFF). The Initech manual documents a separate, narrower prompt behavior.

title: Percent-delimited variables are not expanded at the prompt
steps: Boot advanced-keyboard; SET X=expanded; ECHO %X%.
observed: The output is literally %X%.
expected: Expand the environment reference to expanded (tester DOS command-line memory). Initech documentation only promises expansion in batch files, so this is compatibility, not a false manual-contract claim.

title: DIR includes hidden and system files in normal listings
steps: Boot suite2; run \CASES\B003.BAT. HIDDEN.TXT has +H and SYSTEM.TXT has +S, set by mattrib during fixture preparation.
observed: DIR /W includes HIDDEN.TXT and SYSTEM.TXT; normal and .TXT listings do too.
expected: Omit hidden/system files from ordinary DOS 3.3 DIR output (original DOS Reference DIR pp.57-58; tester attribute expectation).

title: Protected-file redirection reports Bad command
steps: Boot suite2; CD \T; ECHO LOST > READONLY.TXT; ECHO LOST >> READONLY.TXT; TYPE READONLY.TXT.
observed: Both attempts say Bad command or file name. The protected contents remain PROTECTED.
expected: Report Access denied for a protected destination (tester diagnostic expectation; InitechDOS Reference ch2-entries-a.tex:227-228 uses that wording for COPY protection).

title: FDISK labels both mounted primary partitions C:
steps: Boot advanced-fdisk with geometry-boot-fixture.img; FDISK; 4; Enter.
observed: Both partition rows start C:, though the second volume is mounted and accessible as D:. The corrected CHS fixture rules out the earlier bad-cylinder display.
expected: Show C: for the first and D: for the second mapped volume (tester consistency expectation; FDISK partition display).

title: A malformed COM file halts the entire machine
steps: Boot prog-garbage using program-fixture.img; CD \T; GARBAGE.COM. Fixture bytes are 0F 0B (invalid opcode). Try ECHO ALIVE afterwards.
observed: PC LOAD LETTER / ERROR 06 appears; serial reports PANIC vec=06 and HALTED. No prompt returns.
expected: Report the program failure and recover a usable shell (tester robustness expectation for this native hobby OS; not a promise that historical real-mode DOS isolated arbitrary programs). The panic wording itself is deliberate.

title: An unsupported 16-bit MZ file halts without a screen diagnostic
steps: Boot prog-mz16 using program-fixture.img; CD \T; DOS16.EXE. The crafted 32-byte MZ header and tiny 16-bit exit body are in prepare_special.py.
observed: The screen stays on DOS16.EXE with no new prompt/message. Serial says foreign-mz: untagged 16-bit DOS .EXE and HALTED.
expected: Refuse the unsupported format visibly and return to the shell; the brief explicitly requires a loud failure rather than a hang. Executing 16-bit programs is not demanded.
